messages.text: Shop····. DOA NerdQA++. I've been emailing for two weeks without any response.

I am Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Sarah passed me your chat so I can check the unit itself.

Sorry about the two weeks of silence on email, that is not how this should go.

To get this moving, one thing first: when you plug the NerdQaxe++ in with its power brick, what exactly happens?

1. Nothing at all, no screen, no fan, no LED
2. Fan spins and/or screen lights up, but it never hashes (0 GH/s)
3. Screen shows an error or a message

If the screen shows anything, a photo of it helps. "Will not power on" on these boards is most often the power brick rather than the miner, so that is what I want to rule out first.
It beeps/clicks, like it's trying to start up, but maybe is being shutdown for protection. Short on the board? No screen light up. PSU is fine, I tried it on other units.

That clicking with a known-good brick is the right thing to tell me. A repeating click or beep on plug-in with no screen at all usually means the supply is going into protection, which points at the board pulling too much current rather than at the brick.

Leave it unplugged for now, no point retrying it repeatedly.

Two things so I can lock this down:

1. A short video (10 to 15 seconds) of you plugging it in, with the sound, so the click pattern is audible
2. A clear photo of the serial number label on the unit

One more check while you are there: with it unplugged, look at the board around the voltage regulator and the chips for any discoloured, scorched or lifted component, and tell me if you smell anything burnt. If you see or smell anything like that, stop there and do not plug it in again.

Send those over and I will pass my findings straight to the team. They are offline until 10am ET today, and the answer will come to your email.

On the NerdQaxe++ it is usually on a small sticker rather than printed on the board. Check in this order:

1. The underside of the board or the back of the case, a white or silver sticker, often with a QR or barcode
2. The outer box or the antistatic bag it came in, the label there carries the same number
3. If the unit has a plate or backplate, look under it before you unscrew anything

If there is no sticker anywhere, that is fine, do not pull the unit apart to hunt for it. In that case just send me a clear photo of the whole board, front and back. The team can identify the batch from the board revision and the markings.

The video with the click sound is the important one, so send that even if the serial never turns up.

Easiest routes, in order:

1. In this chat, use the attachment or paperclip button and pick the video. Photos always go through; a short video can be too large for the chat
2. If it will not upload, put it on Google Drive, Dropbox, iCloud or YouTube as unlisted, then paste the link here. Make sure the link is set so anyone with it can view
3. Faster still if you want eyes on it right now: our Discord, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , drop the video in and mention @nullhashrate (JD, our hardware lead). He and the community are very active there

Keep it short, 10 to 15 seconds, with the sound on so the click pattern is audible. If the file is big, record it again at a lower resolution, 720p is plenty.

Thanks, the file came through as PXL_20261012_124743438_RMA.mp4, but the link is still private, it asks for a Google sign-in so I cannot open it.

Quick fix on the Drive link:

1. Open the file in Drive, tap Share
2. Under General access, change Restricted to "Anyone with the link"
3. Leave it on Viewer, copy the link again and paste it here

Then I have everything I need. For what it is worth, what you have described already lines up: a clicking or beeping restart loop with no screen, on a power brick you have proven good on other units, is the supply tripping its protection because the board is pulling too much current. That is a board-level fault, not a setting or a firmware problem. The video is so JD, our hardware lead, can confirm the click pattern at a glance.
